explanations: The consumer counts failed attempts in a map keyed by msg.receipt, but the broker issues a new receipt on every delivery. Each redelivery of the failing message looks like its first attempt, so the count never reaches maxAttempts. The message is never dead-lettered and is nacked and redelivered forever, burning CPU and delaying the results queued behind it. Malformed messages still reached the DLQ because they skip the counter. Keying the attempt count by msg.id, which stays the same across redeliveries, makes the third failure dead-letter the message with its body, original id, error and attempt count, which is what redrive needs later.
